title: Board of Pharmacy pharmacist qualifications for collaborative practice
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.02(1), in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b), to qualify to enter into a collaborative practice agreement and engage in collaborative practice a pharmacist must: (a) hold a CURRENT UNRESTRICTED LICENSE IN GOOD STANDING to practice pharmacy in the Commonwealth and currently be engaged in pharmacy practice in the Commonwealth; (b) maintain at least $1,000,000 (PER OCCURRENCE) of professional liability insurance DURING THE TERM OF THE AGREEMENT WHICH SPECIFICALLY COVERS DRUG THERAPY MANAGEMENT; (c) have completed five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist OR have satisfied one of the requirements in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1. through 2., which are 1. have earned a doctor of pharmacy degree AND have entered into a collaborative practice agreement ON OR BEFORE JUNE 30, 2017, or 2. have completed such other education or residency criteria that the Board determines to be the equivalent of five years experience as a licensed pharmacist; (d) devote a portion of practice to the defined drug therapy area that the pharmacist shall co-manage; and (e) complete, in each year of the term of the agreement, at least five additional contact hours of Board-approved continuing education that address areas of practice generally related to THE PARTICULAR collaborative practice agreement. 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) states further conditions, at 247 CMR 16.02(1)(f)1. through 3., if prescriptive practices are included in the agreement.
exam_relevance: Tests the regulation a Massachusetts pharmacist must actually satisfy, which is narrower than the statute on three elements: the doctor of pharmacy route is closed to an agreement entered after June 30, 2017, the licence must be unrestricted and in good standing, and the insurance is per occurrence, maintained during the term, and specific to drug therapy management.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

numeric_facts.fact: professional liability insurance a collaborating pharmacist must maintain
numeric_facts.conditions: per occurrence, maintained during the term of the agreement, specifically covering drug therapy management

numeric_facts.fact: experience as a licensed pharmacist satisfying 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)
numeric_facts.conditions: unless one of the alternatives in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1. through 2. is satisfied

numeric_facts.fact: latest date on which an agreement may have been entered for the doctor of pharmacy route in 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1.
numeric_facts.conditions: the pharmacist must hold a doctor of pharmacy degree and have entered into a collaborative practice agreement on or before that date

numeric_facts.fact: additional Board-approved continuing education under 247 CMR 16.02(1)(e)
numeric_facts.conditions: in each year of the term of the agreement, addressing areas of practice generally related to the particular collaborative practice agreement

exceptions: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c) is satisfied by five years of experience as a licensed pharmacist, or by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)1., a doctor of pharmacy degree together with a collaborative practice agreement entered on or before June 30, 2017, or by 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c)2., other education or residency criteria the Board determines to be the equivalent of five years experience.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(f) applies only if prescriptive practices are included in the collaborative practice agreement.
common_confusions: 247 CMR 16.02(1)(c) is not M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(b)(3) and is not 243 CMR 2.12(2)(c); each of those states a doctor of pharmacy degree as a free-standing alternative to five years of experience, and the Board of Pharmacy regulation does not.
The licence element is a current unrestricted licence in good standing, not merely a current licence.
247 CMR 16.02(1)(e) states five additional contact hours with no continuing education unit alternative, and ties the subject matter to the particular agreement.
verification_notes: Read in the current official publication of 247 CMR 16.00 at the Board of Registration in Pharmacy download link on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule rather than by changing an existing record, so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
